questions.label: Practice · A 69-year-old woman with controlled rheumatoid arthritis takes methotrexate and prednisone 5 mg daily. She develops herpes zoster on her left shoulder and starts oral acyclovir at rash onset. The rash heals, but burning pain in the affected area continues to disrupt sleep more than 90 days after rash onset. Which diagnosis matches this course?

Practice · A 76-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis takes prednisone 7.5 mg daily. Three weeks after starting amitriptyline 25 mg for peripheral neuropathy, she develops hard stools every four to five days with straining. She also takes methotrexate, folic acid, and omeprazole. Examination shows mild abdominal distension and stool in the rectal vault. Which strategy addresses a possible anticholinergic medication contribution while considering an alternative for neuropathic pain?

Practice · A 75-year-old woman with well-controlled rheumatoid arthritis treated with methotrexate attends for influenza vaccination. She has no other major comorbidities and asks about research in which rapamycin improved vaccine responses in older adults. Which pathway effect does Hazzard identify in this research?
Practice · An 81-year-old woman taking methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis develops cytopenia and oral mucosal ulcerations. Which mechanism is listed for this drug in Hazzard's treatment table?

Practice · A 75-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis reports recurrent falls over three months. She takes methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily, and prednisone 10 mg daily, continued for eight months for a flare. Examination shows proximal weakness (hip flexors 3/5), normal reflexes, and cushingoid features. She cannot rise from a chair without using her arms. Her latest DEXA T-score is -3.2. Steroid myopathy is suspected. Which approach targets this suspected adverse effect according to Hazzard?

Practice · A 71-year-old immunosuppressed woman taking methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis presents with painful vulvar ulcers and urinary urgency. She reports no sexual activity. Examination shows multiple shallow ulcers on the labia majora and bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. Which statement about genital HSV is supported by Hazzard?

questions.label: Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and newly diagnosed paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is being assessed for anticoagulation. Her creatinine clearance is in the 30–49 mL/min range. She takes metformin, glipizide, amlodipine, and metoprolol, lives alone, manages daily tasks independently, and sometimes forgets medication doses. If rivaroxaban is selected, which statement agrees with Hazzard's table?

Practice · An 81-year-old man has burning pain and allodynia in the left T10 dermatome six months after herpes zoster. Gabapentin and duloxetine have not helped. He has COPD, atrial fibrillation treated with apixaban, and stage 3 CKD; other medications are metoprolol, tiotropium, and acetaminophen. The pain prevents him from hugging his grandchildren. Which listed coanalgesic appears as a topical patch option in Hazzard’s Table 68-8?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with advanced chronic kidney disease, coronary artery disease, and recently diagnosed colon cancer has severe constipation and cramping abdominal pain after chemotherapy. He takes ondansetron, aspirin, atorvastatin, and metoprolol. Vital signs are stable; the abdomen is distended with hyperactive bowel sounds, and abdominal imaging shows fecal loading without obstruction. Which laxative does Hazzard advise against because of its greater adverse-effect risk in older adults?

Practice · A 90-year-old man with severe COPD on home oxygen, heart failure, and BPH presents with acute urinary retention. Catheterization drains 1.2 liters. His eGFR is 28 mL/min/1.73 m², and he takes furosemide 40 mg twice daily, metoprolol, and finasteride. His urologist proposes GreenLight laser photovaporization (PVP). Which comparison with TURP is supported by Hazzard when discussing the procedure?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with HFpEF (EF 58%), type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and biopsy-proven transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis has NYHA class II symptoms despite furosemide 40 mg daily, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Echocardiography shows LV wall thickening and grade 2 diastolic dysfunction. Which treatment is the TTR stabilizer described in Hazzard as reducing mortality versus placebo in ATTR-ACT?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with new atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc score 4) and stage 3b chronic kidney disease (eGFR 38) starts amiodarone for rhythm control after unsuccessful metoprolol and diltiazem treatment. Baseline QTc is 438 ms. Two weeks later, she develops tremor and heat intolerance. TSH is 0.02, previously 2.1, and free T4 is 3.8 (reference range 0.8–1.8). Which approach best reflects Hazzard's management of amiodarone-associated thyroid dysfunction?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia and atrial fibrillation is reviewed after a mechanical fall at home. His wife reports increasing confusion over the past two weeks and difficulty managing medications. He takes warfarin with a target INR of 2-3, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. His INR today is 4.8, without active bleeding. After addressing the current INR abnormality, the clinician is considering a direct oral anticoagulant for longer-term stroke prevention. Which principle should guide this assessment?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, and a left ventricular ejection fraction below 40% has recurrent activity-limiting episodes despite high-dose metoprolol. Between episodes his heart rate and blood pressure are low. He receives anticoagulation. Which next strategy best fits the source?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman reports dizziness when wearing high-necked sweaters or adjusting necklaces. Yesterday she briefly lost consciousness during hair washing at a salon. She has coronary artery disease treated with stenting and hypertension, and takes aspirin 81 mg daily, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. If contraindications are excluded, which test directly evaluates suspected carotid sinus hypersensitivity?

Practice · A 78-year-old widower is brought by his son for evaluation of erectile dysfunction. He has been unable to achieve an erection for six months, since starting a new medicine. His history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.8%), and major depression after his wife died eight months ago. He takes metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and sertraline 100 mg daily, started six months ago. Blood pressure is 128/76 and heart rate is 62. Which principle should guide medication assessment before choosing a replacement antidepressant?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with stable coronary disease, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) had his last myocardial infarction three years ago. He takes aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metformin 1000 mg twice daily. LDL is 72 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.8%. His wife reports missed evening doses. Which prescribing approach directly addresses the regimen-complexity problem described by Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old man has frailty with unintentional 15-lb weight loss, exhaustion, weakness, and slow walking speed, and stage 3b CKD (eGFR 36). He takes 12 medications, including atorvastatin 80 mg, aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 40 mg. Blood pressure is 108/64 and albumin 3.1. Which approach follows Hazzard's principles for reviewing this medication burden?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes, coronary artery disease, and depression presents with dizziness and weakness. He takes metformin, atorvastatin, metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, lisinopril, paroxetine 40 mg daily, and recently added amitriptyline 75 mg for neuropathy. BP is 102/68 seated and 84/52 standing, heart rate is 58, and QTc is 492 ms. Which assessment of amitriptyline follows from the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman who lives alone and manages her medications was independent in basic ADLs until three days ago. Her daughter finds her acutely confused and inattentive. Temperature is 37.1°C, heart rate 88/min, blood pressure 108/62 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 20/min. She is oriented to person only and repeatedly asks when her husband, who died two years ago, will arrive. Medications include donepezil 10 mg, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and zolpidem 10 mg nightly, started one week ago. Which interpretation should guide the initial assessment?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with a myocardial infarction 12 years ago, chronic stable angina, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease attends a medication review. He functions well and walks two miles daily without symptoms. He takes aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, amlodipine 5 mg, and atorvastatin 40 mg. Blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg, heart rate is 64 beats/min, and a recent echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 55%. Before deciding whether to deprescribe metoprolol, which finding would support deprescribing under Hazzard's framework?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with NYHA class II heart failure, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment wants to begin exercising. He lives alone, has fallen twice in the past year, and takes metformin, lisinopril, and metoprolol. His daughter is concerned about safety. Which approach best applies Hazzard's exercise principles?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with COPD, coronary artery disease, and chronic pain from lumbar spinal stenosis has increasing dyspnea that limits him to climbing one flight of stairs. He takes formoterol/budesonide, tiotropium, aspirin, metoprolol, and oxycodone 5 mg four times daily. Spirometry is unchanged from baseline, with FEV1 35% predicted. His MRC dyspnea score is 3/5 and cardiac evaluation is negative. Which statement should guide referral for pulmonary rehabilitation?

Practice · A 91-year-old man in supported housing with mild dementia (MMSE 22) has lost 3 kg over two months. Staff report that he refuses denture care and eats soft foods. His upper denture fits poorly, with marked ridge resorption and several denture-associated pressure ulcers. His daughter asks about implants. Creatinine clearance is 45 mL/min; medications include donepezil and metoprolol. Which principle should guide initial management of the suspected denture trauma?

Practice · A 70-year-old woman with heart failure, diabetes, and arthritis reports that her medications are affecting sexual function. She takes metoprolol, furosemide, metformin, and gabapentin for neuropathic pain and asks about changing treatment. Which approach best reflects the source's discussion of medication-related sexual concerns in older women?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman with heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), atrial fibrillation treated with warfarin, and mild cognitive impairment lives alone. Her daughter reports medication errors, including duplicate doses. She takes warfarin 5 mg daily, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, and digoxin 0.125 mg daily. INR is 5.8 and digoxin level is 2.4 ng/mL. She is alert but confused about the date. Which intervention best prevents another duplicate dose at home?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman has peripheral arterial disease (ABI 0.45), stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22), and a recent fall with hip fracture. Claudication now limits walking to 50 feet, and duplex shows 80% superficial femoral artery stenosis. She takes clopidogrel 75 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. When planning exercise within her safe capabilities, which walking approach is described for claudication?

Practice · An 83-year-old man with heart failure, stage 3b CKD (eGFR 35), and mild dementia is receiving hospice care for end-stage heart disease. Severe peripheral edema is causing skin breakdown and discomfort. He takes morphine 5 mg every four hours and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. His wife asks whether a diuretic could help. Which approach follows the source treatment of symptomatic congestion?

Practice · A 76-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and chronic back pain has become sedentary and mentally foggy despite physical therapy. He takes duloxetine, cyclobenzaprine, and acetaminophen. Which medication change best reduces his anticholinergic and sedative burden?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 24) and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) is hospitalized with pneumonia. On day three she develops acute confusion, visual hallucinations, and agitation; the CAM is positive. She pulls at an indwelling urinary catheter that is no longer medically needed. She is receiving levofloxacin, acetaminophen, amlodipine, and atorvastatin. Which initial intervention best follows Hazzard’s nonpharmacologic approach?

Practice · An 82-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced dementia and breast cancer metastatic to bone presents with two days of shouting, agitation, food refusal, and pulling at her clothes. She is nonverbal at baseline and grimaces during abdominal palpation. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, heart rate 88, and blood pressure 142/78. She receives memantine 10 mg twice daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. Which approach best addresses the acute behavioral change?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment, hypertension, and osteoarthritis attends routine follow-up. Her daughter reports frequent liquid stool soiling despite complaints of constipation. Medications include amlodipine 5 mg, acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and docusate 100 mg twice daily. Digital rectal examination reveals a large mass of hard stool in the rectal vault with liquid stool leaking around it. Lawton-Brody assessment shows new difficulty shopping and preparing meals. What is the preferred initial approach?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman with moderate vascular dementia in a memory-care unit has refused bathing for two weeks and smells of urine. She becomes aggressive when approached with bathing equipment, but there is no immediate danger. She has hypertension and osteoarthritis and takes amlodipine 5 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg twice daily. Her daughter says she used to be meticulous about cleanliness. Alongside assessing causes of distress, which approach follows first-line behavioral care?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with hypertension and osteoarthritis develops fatigue and exertional dyspnea after starting meloxicam for knee pain. Hemoglobin is 8.2 g/dL, MCV 78 fL, ferritin 18 ng/mL, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL from 1.1, and eGFR 32 mL/min/1.73 m². Stool testing is positive for blood and colonoscopy shows a bleeding diverticulum. After the acute bleed is treated, which analgesic principle follows Hazzard's discussion of safer prescribing for osteoarthritis?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter and needs help with IADLs. On the third hospital day for pneumonia she is more confused at night, sleeps during the day, is oriented to person, and picks at unseen objects. CAM is positive. She receives ceftriaxone 1 g daily and acetaminophen as needed. Alongside evaluating and treating causes, which environmental approach is consistent with delirium and sleep-wake management?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with severe osteoarthritis and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52; Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance 38) has inadequate relief from acetaminophen 1 g three times daily. She has hypertension and heart failure with an ejection fraction of 45%, and takes lisinopril, carvedilol, and furosemide. If an opioid trial is warranted after other treatments have been reviewed, which agent does Hazzard place before other opioids?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with Alzheimer dementia (MMSE 14) and osteoarthritis has fallen twice in the past month without injury. She inconsistently uses a walker. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg four times daily; amitriptyline 25 mg nightly was added for sleep six weeks ago. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/68 after three minutes standing; pulse rises from 72 to 78. Which medication change best addresses the timing of the falls and the postural pressure drop?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman hospitalized with pneumonia becomes irritable on the third hospital day, grimaces with movement, and resists care. She has moderate dementia, a positive delirium screen, and difficulty localizing her reported severe generalized pain. Temperature is 37.8°C, heart rate 102, and blood pressure 160/95. Her home medications include donepezil, amlodipine, and acetaminophen 500 mg twice daily for arthritis. While evaluating the new pain and delirium, the team considers acetaminophen as one component of treatment for her osteoarthritis pain. Which approach follows Hazzard’s discussion of this drug?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with hypertension, diabetes, osteoarthritis, and newly diagnosed mild cognitive impairment takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, celecoxib 200 mg daily, and acetaminophen 500 mg four times daily. She develops ankle edema, an eight-pound weight gain over two weeks, and worsening knee pain. Blood pressure is 165/95 mm Hg, pulse 88/min, and creatinine has risen from 1.1 to 1.4 mg/dL. Which change directly removes an NSAID exposure while retaining a non-NSAID analgesic strategy?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman with diabetes, stage 4 CKD, and peripheral neuropathy has severe burning foot pain despite gabapentin and acetaminophen. She has also developed confusion and fallen. Which step best applies Hazzard's medication-safety principles before adding or escalating treatment?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with chronic low-back pain has marked lumbar facet arthropathy on MRI, local facet tenderness, and pain on extension and lateral rotation. She has hypertension and osteoporosis and takes amlodipine, alendronate, and acetaminophen. Physical therapy gave little relief, and tramadol caused nausea. Which description of medial branch blocks agrees with Hazzard?

Practice · אישה בת 84 עם יתר לחץ דם, כאב כרוני עקב היצרות עמוד השדרה, ו-MCI שאובחן לאחרונה, מגיעה עם בתה לחידוש מרשמים. היא נוטלת amlodipine 5mg, gabapentin 300mg TID, ו-acetaminophen PRN. הבת עונה על כל השאלות ומפסיקה את המטופלת בכל פעם שהיא מנסה לדבר. כשנשאלת על שליטה בכאב, המטופלת מתחילה לענות אך הבת מתערבת ואומרת 'היא בסדר, היא מתלוננת יותר מדי.' המטופלת מורידה את עיניה ומפסיקה לדבר. איזה סוג של התעללות הכי סביר במקרה זה?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer disease and osteoarthritis has increased evening confusion and fell a week ago. He takes donepezil 10 mg nightly, memantine 10 mg twice daily, acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and amitriptyline 50 mg nightly for chronic pain. Which action directly addresses a strongly anticholinergic medication exposure?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%), mild cognitive impairment, and knee osteoarthritis is hospitalized with decompensated heart failure. She lives alone and is independent in four of six activities of daily living. Her discharge medications include furosemide 40 mg twice daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, and naproxen 500 mg twice daily for knee pain. Creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL and eGFR is 28 mL/min/1.73 m². If an oral analgesic is still needed after non-drug measures, which initial change best fits the approach on Hazzard p312?
Practice · A care-home resident with dementia and behavioral problems is assessed for possible pain. What was the first step in the empiric stepwise pain-treatment protocol described in Hazzard?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman with heart failure, mild dementia, and osteoarthritis presents with weight loss and fatigue. After a fall, she moved in with her daughter. She takes furosemide, lisinopril, donepezil, and acetaminophen. She eats less and needs medication reminders. Her weight fell from 58 to 52 kg in six months; albumin is 3.0 and thyroid function is normal. Which approach reflects comprehensive geriatric assessment?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with mild Alzheimer dementia and osteoarthritis spends more time in bed, eats less, and has lost interest in weekly card games. She has near-falls when reaching, temporal wasting, loose clothing, and difficulty rising from the examination table. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. She has lost 12 lb (8%) in six months; TSH is normal, B12 is 320 pg/mL, and albumin is 3.4 g/dL. Which exercise prescription best addresses her weakness?

Practice · An 85-year-old assisted-living resident with moderate Alzheimer disease is on day three after hip-fracture repair. After sleeping well on earlier nights, she is now awake, repeatedly getting out of bed, and saying she must get the children ready for school. She takes memantine 10 mg twice daily, vitamin D, acetaminophen as needed, and zolpidem 5 mg at bedtime added last night. Vital signs are normal. Which medication change follows Beers 2023 guidance for the new delirium?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman in assisted living is assessed because her care needs have increased. She has moderate Alzheimer disease, osteoporosis with a recent vertebral fracture, and urinary incontinence. Her caregiver reports new dependence in bathing and dressing, previously performed independently, and two falls this month. Her medicines are donepezil 10 mg daily, alendronate 70 mg weekly, oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, and acetaminophen as needed. Which response to oxybutynin matches Beers 2023?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, hypertension and osteoarthritis is assessed after a fall in assisted living. He takes carbidopa/levodopa, amlodipine and as-needed acetaminophen. Examination shows masked facies and cogwheel rigidity, with a marked fall in blood pressure and dizziness on standing. Which approach fits the described treatment principles for orthostatic hypotension?
